observations: Two separate sewing machine stands are shown in an outdoor setting.
The stand on the left has a blue painted top surface with a decorative wave pattern.
The stand on the right has a brown wood-grain painted top surface.
Both stands feature the classic cast iron treadle frame design with a foot pedal and a lower metal grate.
The top surface of the blue stand in photo 2 has a metal ruler attached to its edge.
The top surface of the brown stand in photo 3 has a glass insert in the center.
The stands appear to be in good structural condition but show signs of outdoor exposure.

claims.evidence: The cast iron frames and treadle mechanisms shown in photos 0, 1, 2, and 3 are characteristic of sewing machine stands.

risks.risk: The stands may be missing the sewing machine heads or the treadle wheels may be seized.
risks.proof: A video showing the treadle wheels being turned and the machine head moving.

risks.risk: The paint on the tops may be peeling or the wood-grain finish may be a poor replica.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the painted surfaces without glare.
risks.if_unproven: as painted surfaces with potential chipping

risks.risk: The metal ruler on the blue stand may be a decorative addition rather than a functional measuring tool.
risks.proof: A photo of the ruler with a handwritten measurement.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the treadle wheels being operated to confirm they are not seized.
Close-up photos of the painted surfaces to check for peeling or poor quality.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as sewing machine legs. They can be priced at their worst-case value as incomplete stands without heads, assuming the treadle wheels are functional.
